h: A Forest Next Door and a Market Town Down the Road
p: Birdworld sits beside Alice Holt Forest, a big Forestry England woodland just south of Farnham, and that's one of the best things about it. When you've had your fill of feathers, the forest has walking and cycling trails, play trails for little ones and a Go Ape treetop course for braver older kids, so you can stretch a half-day into a full one without moving the car very far.

It's a brilliant pairing because the two are so different. Birdworld is all about getting close to colourful species from faraway places, while the forest lets children run, climb and spot British wildlife in the wild. Keep your eyes open for woodland birds as well; after a morning learning about penguins and parrots, it's surprising how much more children notice a robin or a woodpecker.

Farnham itself is a handsome Georgian market town with an old castle keep on the hill above the streets. The Farnham Maltings, a former malting building, is now an arts centre that hosts markets, shows and events. Just outside town, the ruins of Waverley Abbey, the first Cistercian abbey in England, sit beside the River Wey and make a peaceful stop.

Plan on a decent pair of trainers, a waterproof and a picnic. The road down from Farnham runs towards Bordon, so if you're coming from the M3 or A31 it's a straightforward drive. Birdworld is also a good one for budding bird-watchers of any age. Bring a small notebook and let the kids keep a tally of the birds they spot, both inside the park and out in the forest afterwards.
